The skies have changed, so has IAF's mission: 94 years of India's air power
articles.summary: Raised on 8 October 1932, the Indian Air Force began with four Westland Wapiti biplanes and five Indian pilots at Drigh Road, Karachi. Today it is the world's fourth-largest air force, operating fighters such as the Su-30MKI, Rafale and Tejas, though it fields around 29 fighter squadrons against a sanctioned 42. Its combat record spans the Second World War, the wars of 1947-48, 1965 and 1971, Kargil, Balakot and Operation Sindoor. The force is now evolving into a networked aerospace power, built around the Integrated Air Command and Control System, growing unmanned capabilities and long-range airlift. That reach extends to multinational exercises such as Tarang Shakti and humanitarian missions as far afield as Venezuela, underlining its expanding strategic role.

articles.title: 3 years, 50,000 rifles later: Why US Army is moving on from the M7

articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has revealed why he left Portugal’s camp, claiming Jorge Jesus broke promises over his playing time and then contradicted their private agreement publicly. Ronaldo said the situation left him feeling unwanted and that continuing would harm the team. He apologised for leaving, accepted responsibility for his actions and insisted he remains available to compete for Portugal after his suspension.

articles.title: Storm stranded wedding guests, so 400 strangers showed up to celebrate
articles.summary: Amidst the storm, Kimberly Laprad and Jayden Sink transformed their wedding on Hatteras Island into a community affair when their guests were unable to make it. Inviting locals resulted in an impressive turnout of 500 to 800 attendees who came together to support the couple. Local businesses generously provided food and services while the couple looks forward to returning every year to contribute to community initiatives.

articles.title: Supreme Court revives grower's claim after police destroyed $37K legal hemp
articles.summary: In 2021, Georgia police aircraft allegedly destroyed $37,000 worth of legally grown hemp during a drug-suppression operation. Six years later, the Georgia Supreme Court revived the grower’s compensation claim, overturning a 60-year-old precedent that broadly shielded government agencies from property-damage claims when acting under police powers. The ruling allows the lawsuit to proceed, though damages have not yet been awarded.

articles.title: NYC Mayor wants AI to be regulated at every single level; points to layoffs and more
articles.summary: In a bold statement, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has called for stringent regulations on artificial intelligence. Highlighting a troubling 10 percent risk of human extinction according to certain experts, he insists that national supervision is crucial to navigate AI’s societal effects. Mamdani also raises concerns about job market disruptions and the ways individuals interact with information, challenging the prevailing narrative of an AI arms race with China.

articles.title: IIM-A gold medallist now leads 13-member Microsoft team in Canada
articles.summary: Shubham Goyal graduated with distinction from IIM Ahmedabad, but his true passion has always been learning rather than chasing medals. After completing his studies, he joined Boston Consulting Group, gaining essential business acumen. Transitioning to Microsoft, he initially dove into product management before leading the enterprise deployment of Microsoft Security solutions. Goyal stresses that true career fulfillment lies in ongoing education and personal growth, not just financial rewards.

articles.title: 'Will call Putin over pneumonic plague,' says Trump - what is happening in Russia?
articles.summary: A woman at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia reportedly died from pneumonia of unknown cause. While there are suggestions she may have contracted pneumonic plague, Russian authorities have not confirmed this diagnosis. The World Health Organisation assesses the risk of spreading beyond Russia as very low and is in contact with Russian officials. US President Donald Trump plans to discuss the case with Russian President Vladimir Putin soon.

articles.title: AAP neta claims wife posed as PCS officer, hid previous marriage, 18-year-old son
articles.summary: Amarinder Singh Mandofal, an AAP functionary, was duped into marrying a woman posing as a PCS officer. She concealed her previous marriage and departed with gold and cash, raising suspicion. Mandofal discovered her forged documents, including certificates and identification. Her family allegedly threatened him over a settlement due to concealed facts. Police have registered an FIR against the woman and five relatives while the investigation continues.

articles.title: All 10 Rajya Sabha candidates from UP set to get elected unopposed
articles.summary: In the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections, all 10 candidates from BJP and Samajwadi Party are set to be elected unopposed. Samajwadi Party decided against fielding a third candidate, eliminating the possibility of a contest. The BJP is positioned to secure all eight available seats due to its majority in the Assembly. The results will be formally declared after the nomination scrutiny concludes on October 9.

articles.title: Gujarat: Married woman, lover forced into public sex as ‘punishment’
articles.summary: A shocking incident occurred in Surendranagar where a couple was subjected to horrific punishment by the woman's husband. After the couple was located, police arrested nine individuals involved in the brutal acts. The couple was reportedly filmed during the ordeal, which was shared on social media. Authorities were alerted by local community leaders who facilitated the police intervention.

articles.title: Brent crosses $101 as Saudi attacks, US storm add to oil supply concerns
articles.summary: Rising oil prices, now exceeding 1%, raise alarms over potential storm disruptions affecting U.S. oil production and refineries. With Brent crude passing $101 per barrel and WTI crude hitting $90.38, concerns are amplified by supply issues from Saudi Arabia and mixed signals on U.S. inventories. Coupled with ongoing tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, analysts predict sustained high prices unless significant diplomatic progress is made.

articles.title: Who is Anirudh Thapa, only the second Indian to score against Uruguay in 44 years?
articles.summary: India’s 6–1 defeat to Uruguay was painful, but Anirudh Thapa provided a rare moment of history by ending the country’s 44-year wait for a goal against La Celeste. His rebound made him only the second Indian scorer against Uruguay, joining Manas Bhattacharya, who struck in 1982. For Thapa, the landmark goal also marked his first international strike since 2023.

articles.title: Teen couple commit suicide on Instagram live in Dahod forest; family among viewers
articles.summary: A man named Rajesh Ninama and a 16-year-old girl ended their lives in Dahod district. They livestreamed the act on Instagram, leaving viewers horrified and their families devastated. Rajesh had approached his parents for permission to marry the girl, but they refused due to clan differences. Following this rejection, the couple decided to take their own lives in a forested area.

articles.title: 'Against all odds': Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike awake after failed execution
articles.summary: Christa Pike, a death row inmate in Tennessee, is recovering at a hospital following a failed execution attempt. Her lawyers reported that she is awake and speaking after being unconscious for several days. Doctors say the extent of her recovery remains uncertain, and she might face a long rehabilitation process. Legal questions arise about whether Tennessee can execute her again after the failed lethal injection.

articles.title: Drishyam 3 crosses Rs 216 cr in 5 days, nears Drishyam 2 record
articles.summary: ‘Drishyam 3’ has earned Rs 216.50 crore net in India in five days, with Rs 19 crore on Tuesday. Ajay Devgn's thriller opened at a career-best Rs 62 crore, has doubled the original's lifetime total, and sits about Rs 30 crore short of Drishyam 2's Rs 239.67 crore record.

articles.title: Most GST refunds may be processed within 17 days
articles.summary: The GST Council intends to shorten the refund processing period to around 17 days for businesses. It will also work to automate registering for a GST number to speed up the process. For small businesses operating in multiple states, avoiding repetitive registrations will be considered. Additionally, the proposal includes eliminating physical verification for registration cancellations. Changes will allow input tax credit on various business-related expenses to facilitate smoother operations.

articles.title: 'North by Northwest' star Eva Marie Saint passes away at 102
articles.summary: Eva Marie Saint, the acclaimed actress famed for her iconic role in ‘On the Waterfront’, has sadly passed away at her Los Angeles residence, surrounded by her loving family. Born on July 4, 1924, in Newark, New Jersey, she was raised in Albany and Delmar, New York. Throughout her illustrious career, Saint captivated audiences with her performances in numerous films and television series, earning a multitude of prestigious awards.

articles.title: 80% vote in West Bengal bypolls amid rigging, intimidation charges

In Tamil Nadu, turnout dipped compared to previous elections, with results showing 86% and 80% participation. Assam's Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency recorded 76% turnout during the bypolls, while Puducherry's Thattanchavady seat had a turnout of 78% by 5pm. Various candidates and parties reported incidents of interference and blocked agents during the polling process.

articles.title: Meet Monarchs: ‘Endangered’ traveller butterflies that survive on poisonous milkweed
articles.summary: The extraordinary migration of monarch butterflies stretches across thousands of miles, connecting North America and Mexico. Sadly, their population has sharply declined, prompting the International Union for Conservation of Nature to mark them as endangered. Key threats include habitat loss, pesticide usage, and climate change, which disproportionately impact their crucial milkweed supply. To aid these delicate creatures, conservation efforts are imperative, with U.S. federal protection still pending.

articles.title: Ukrainian drone attack sets fire to oil tanker carrying 23 Indians off Russia
articles.summary: The Aframax Rio tanker caught fire off the Russian coast after an attack by unmanned vessels. All 23 crew members onboard, who were Indian nationals, were successfully rescued by emergency crews. The incident occurred near Sochi, leading to the closure of beaches in the area. Authorities monitored air and water quality, assuring safety for public health.

articles.title: Flydubai cockpit attack left Capt Smit Machchhar with 'depressed skull fracture'
articles.summary: Captain Smit Machchhar faced serious injuries from his co-pilot during the flight's crisis situation. The co-pilot attacked him with an axe, resulting in a skull fracture that required emergency surgery. Doctors monitored his recovery closely and assisted him for further treatment in the UAE. The Indian embassy is providing support to Captain Machchhar and his family during this challenging time.

articles.title: Opposition's anti-SIR-CEC march turns into INDIA bloc-government face-off
articles.summary: Opposition members from the INDIA bloc, led by Rahul Gandhi, organized a protest march to the Election Commission. The police stopped their march just before reaching Akashvani Bhavan, leading to a lengthy dharna by the MPs. Despite police attempts to remove the protesters, several MPs entered the Akashvani premises and continued their demonstration. Rahul Gandhi criticized Prime Minister Modi and accused his government of treasonous actions against the country.

articles.title: CBI raids CM Bhagwant Mann’s camp office, his OSD’s home in graft probe
articles.summary: CBI conducted raids on multiple locations including the camp office of Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann. The investigation stems from a High Court order based on allegations from the Enforcement Directorate. Various individuals are named in the FIR for their alleged involvement in corruption and manipulation of government processes. Mann criticized the timing of the raids as politically motivated amid upcoming elections.

articles.title: From Gujarat CM to India's PM: Modi's 25 years in office
articles.summary: Narendra Modi's journey began with his role as Gujarat Chief Minister, addressing state issues and implementing reforms. His tenure included launching significant initiatives like the Jan Dhan Yojana and Swachh Bharat Mission, aimed at improving welfare. The BJP's political maneuvers led to Modi becoming Prime Minister in 2014, marking a significant shift in governance.

articles.summary: In one such case in Chennai, a man received cash gifts of Rs 85.03 lakh from his relatives. The Income Tax Department began making enquiries into the source of the Rs 85.03 lakh deposited by the man. The department also sent tax notices to the relatives who had given him the cash.  The man eventually won relief in ITAT Chennai.

articles.title: Rajnath launches first desi fleet support ship ‘Surya’ at Visakhapatnam
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh launched ‘Surya’, India’s first indigenously-built fleet support ship in Visakhapatnam. He also laid the keel for the fifth ship in the series and inaugurated upgraded infrastructure at Hindustan Shipyard Limited. These developments aim to enhance the Indian Navy’s operational capabilities and self-reliance in naval shipbuilding. Additionally, Rajnath announced the establishment of a second production line for Shakti engines in Koraput.

articles.title: Punjab govt moves SC against CBI probe into ‘bribe syndicate’ linked to Mann OSD

They aim to challenge a High Court order that mandated a CBI investigation into corruption allegations. The High Court's concerns include alleged coercive actions by the Central Bureau of Investigation in the state. The Punjab government argues that the orders violate governance principles outlined in the Constitution.

articles.title: Michael Douglas recalls affairs with co-stars; being 'caught in bed'

He recounts an affair with Jeanne Tripplehorn during the filming of 'Basic Instinct'. The actor also reflects on being caught by his wife in a compromising situation, which led to an ultimatum. articles.title: Oklahoma meteor crater found to be nearly 100 million years younger
articles.summary: Researchers from the University of Texas at Austin have traced the Ames meteor impact to approximately 370 million years ago, presenting a significant revision to the previously accepted estimate of 467 million years. This research connects the impact with the Frasnian-Famennian mass extinction event, employing zircon crystals to establish a more precise timeline, thus providing deeper insights into pivotal moments in Earth's geological history.

articles.title: Moon samples reveal magnetic mineral never before seen naturally
articles.summary: A groundbreaking discovery by researchers has unveiled a new magnetic mineral, γ-Fe, found in lunar samples from the Chang'e-6 mission. This remarkable find sheds light on the ancient magnetic environment of the Moon, now long lost. Detailed analysis of tiny iron particles within lunar impact glasses reveals that γ-Fe can maintain stable magnetic signals, potentially serving as a record of the Moon's magnetic history.

During the protests, BJP representatives criticized Rahul Gandhi and questioned the credibility of his claims about member attendance. The fake doctor has been impersonating a medical professional for nearly three decades while receiving substantial donations. Investigations revealed kickbacks were paid, with funds returned to donors after deducting commissions.

Student commuting patterns differ significantly, with 37% walking to educational institutions.

articles.title: In a record, over 10,000 women clear JEE-Advanced
articles.summary: Women's success rate in JEE-Advanced achieved a record high in 2026 while their IIT seat share remained mostly unchanged. A total of 10,107 women qualified, reflecting a 7.5% increase in their qualifying count. Admissions across IITs reached 18,861, with 20% allocated to female candidates. Significant gains were reported for SC and ST candidates in qualification rates.

articles.title: Supreme Court agreed to meet, then changed mind: ONOE panel chief
articles.summary: The Supreme Court initially planned an informal meeting with the parliamentary committee on simultaneous elections. However, the meeting was canceled after opposition MPs raised concerns about the appropriateness of the interaction. The Supreme Court expressed that discussing the matter could lead to future judicial review. The proposal for the meeting was suggested by DMK MP P Wilson.

articles.title: Pahalgam handler rallies LeT support via anti-Israel rhetoric
articles.summary: Saifullah Kasuri made controversial remarks regarding the Pakistan army's role in regional conflicts. He threatened to erase Israel from the world map and defend Saudi holy sites. After the Pahalgam attack, he has been active in public events to raise support. High-level meetings between Lashkar-e-Taiba and Hamas have been reported, indicating growing connections. Kasuri's actions reflect an increasing boldness post-attack, as he recruits youth and gathers funds.

articles.title: Visa doesn't create absolute right to enter India, says Delhi High Court
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court emphasized that foreign nationals do not have an inherent right to enter India. Justice Amit Mahajan pointed out that holding a visa does not ensure unconditional admission. The court noted various factors that could lead to denial of entry, including national security and public health. A plea by a Turkmenistan woman for reasons regarding her entry refusal was dismissed.

articles.title: Legislative privilege vs free speech: Supreme Court 7-judge bench may close case
articles.summary: Nearly 23 years after the Tamil Nadu assembly's breach of privilege resolution, a Supreme Court hearing is scheduled. The resolution imposed a 15-day sentence on some journalists but has since been withdrawn. Senior advocates claimed that the writ petition's cause of action no longer exists and argued the matter has become academic. As a result, the Supreme Court is expected to dispose of the petitions.

articles.title: World entering age of flux, India will rise to challenges: EAM S Jaishankar
articles.summary: S Jaishankar emphasized the uncertainties facing the world during his speech at the Kautilya Economic Conclave. He expressed confidence in India's ability to navigate challenges such as conflicts and economic volatility. The minister highlighted India's proactive stance during crises, including the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing geopolitical tensions. Jaishankar called for diplomacy to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict, particularly concerning maritime security.

articles.title: Rawat seeks meet with Congress brass as Kumari Selja slams his yatra plan
articles.summary: Harish Rawat's thanksgiving yatra has prompted a strong response from AICC, emphasizing the need for party unity. Kumari Selja has criticized the yatra as a parallel program that undermines Congress interests. The party leadership has expressed concern regarding Rawat's controversial statements and the potential division of support. A meeting between Rawat and Selja is expected to take place later this week.

articles.title: Supreme Court may get 3 judges today, to be one short of full strength
articles.summary: The Union law ministry has announced the appointment of three judges to the Supreme Court. Justice Sunita Agarwal, Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh have been elevated. These judges were previously chief justices of their respective high courts and will be sworn in soon. With these appointments, the Supreme Court remains one judge short of its sanctioned strength.

articles.title: Form 6 not modified, only declaration added: Election Commission
articles.summary: Election Commission officials clarified that there was no change to Form 6, only an additional declaration form was introduced. This statement followed CJI Surya Kant's observation regarding the approval of modified Form 6. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi accused the Chief Election Commissioner of making illegal changes to the form. The Election Commission denied these accusations and referred to a previous press note for clarification.

articles.summary: Three years after the 7 October Hamas attack, Israel's relations with Arab countries remain deeply divided. While it maintains diplomatic ties with the UAE, Egypt, Jordan and Bahrain, the Gaza war and regional conflicts have strained old partnerships and complicated prospects for new ones.

articles.summary: Starting from 1 October, pet parents may be fined  ₹10,000 if their cat or dog is found abandoned in Chennai. &nbsp;The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) plans to track down owners of lost or abandoned pets by scanning their microchips, which is currently mandatory for all pets in the city.

articles.summary: The existing telecom PLI scheme, launched in February 2021, incentivizes local production of network switches, transmission gear, and set-top boxes over a five-year period ending as late as FY27. However, the scheme has seen uneven adoption.

articles.title: Pakistan, Saudi, Turkiye activate Mecca defence pact as Yemen war escalates
articles.summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to enhance military cooperation to address regional security threats. Following recent attacks by Yemen's Houthi group, the three countries will activate collective deterrence measures. The emergency meeting of the Mecca Defence Alliance in Riyadh led to this commitment. Saudi-backed forces are also launching an offensive against the Houthis in Yemen to regain control.

articles.title: SIR row: Will annul EC orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has asked the Election Commission to clarify decision-making processes related to voter roll revisions. It emphasized that decisions should be taken unanimously or by majority among commission members only. Senior advocate Vikas Singh argued for preserving records and scrutiny of the commission's actions. The court will examine allegations of unilateral actions against the Chief Election Commissioner.

articles.title: India, Switzerland eye deeper ties in trade, investment, tech
articles.summary: India and Switzerland have signed five agreements to strengthen cooperation in trade and mobility. The two countries aim to enhance market access for Indian exports and attract Swiss investments in key sectors. A new mobility agreement will facilitate easier access for Indian professionals and students to Switzerland. Both leaders discussed global conflicts and emphasized the importance of dialogue for peace.

articles.title: Not now daal-ing, says MAGA, as Montana governor comes to India to sell pulses
articles.summary: Montana's Governor Greg Gianforte is heading a delegation to India to promote agricultural exports. The focus is on selling lentils, peas, and chickpeas to the world's largest consumer of pulses. This trip highlights the growing tension within the Republican party regarding international trade and immigration. Many in the GOP criticize Gianforte's outreach to India amidst concerns about jobs for Americans.

articles.title: Two killed, Indian among injured after Russian drone hits Turkish cargo ship
articles.summary: A Russian drone struck the MV Royad Mammadov cargo vessel in the Black Sea, resulting in two fatalities. Among the crew were three Indian nationals, one of whom sustained injuries and received medical care. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy confirmed that the ship's captain was killed in the attack and expressed condolences. Romanian authorities responded to the incident by rescuing 11 crew members and recovering two deceased individuals.

articles.title: In 2009, Google’s Eric Schmidt bought a ship; by 2022, it mapped 1.3m sq km of seafloor
articles.summary: In 2009, Eric and Wendy Schmidt took a significant step in marine conservation by acquiring a fisheries protection vessel, rebranding it as Falkor. This vessel became a hub for oceanographic research and exploration, hosting over 1,000 scientists and charting more than 1.3 million square kilometers of the ocean by 2022.

articles.title: Probe sex assault case against Nagina MP Azad, court directs Delhi cops
articles.summary: A Delhi court has ordered the completion of an inquiry into a sexual assault complaint against Chandrashekhar Azad. The complainant accused Azad of raping her under the pretext of marriage and claimed the police did not register an FIR. The police sought additional time for the inquiry, but the complainant opposed this request. The court rejected the police's plea and emphasized that the alleged offence is punishable with life imprisonment.

articles.title: Woman declares Rs 67.4L ancestral jewellery in ITR; gets notice, she wins in ITAT
articles.summary: The assessment threw up two separate issues. The first concerned jewellery worth Rs 67,39,949 that the woman had disclosed in Schedule AL of her income tax return. The tribunal also examined whether the Rs 12 lakh paid to the HUF represented a genuine brokerage expense when the same person, the HUF's Karta/coparcener, had already received another Rs 12 lakh for the same transaction.

articles.title: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR
articles.summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan raised concerns regarding the deletion of voters through special intensive revision, facing criticism from former CJI BR Gavai. While Bhuyan emphasized that disenfranchising citizens violates constitutional rights, Gavai expressed reservations about commenting on ongoing legal matters. Former Supreme Court judge Rohinton Fali Nariman also voiced concerns about the democratic implications of voters being removed from lists.

articles.title: Rajya Sabha polls: 8 fresh BJP faces for UP, Hardeep Puri among 2 ministers dropped
articles.summary: BJP has chosen not to renominate Union ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma for Rajya Sabha. This decision raises speculation about a possible reshuffle of the council of ministers by PM Narendra Modi. Since several ministers have been given organization roles, it indicates their continuation in government may be unlikely. Puri's term ends in November, and he may be reassigned for the Punjab assembly polls.

articles.title: Mission Shakti: How India’s 2019 anti-sat missile test in space caught US off guard
articles.summary: India conducted an unexpected anti-satellite missile test in 2019, which surprised US security agencies completely. The former NRO officer David Grusch recounted his experiences during the incident on a podcast. India announced its capability after destroying a defunct satellite, making it the fourth country to achieve such technology. This test led to concerns about debris affecting US satellites in orbit.

articles.title: California family’s 6,625-acre cattle ranch protected after 112 years
articles.summary: The Kinsey family has strategically safeguarded their vast 6,625-acre ranch in Benbow, California, by implementing a conservation easement. This crucial step preserves the land's agricultural, forest, and wildlife values, ensuring the ranch's ongoing functionality while protecting vital habitats for endangered species. David Johnson, a family member, was instrumental in this initiative, with the Northcoast Regional Land Trust planning to acknowledge their dedication to conservation this coming October.

articles.title: NSW planted bitou bush in 1946; decades later, it spread across 46% of coast
articles.summary: Bitou bush was intentionally planted along the New South Wales coast to stabilize sand dunes. This plant has since spread extensively, covering 46% of the coastline and threatening native vegetation. Infestations of bitou bush replace native plant species and alter animal habitats throughout the region. A Threat Abatement Plan has been established to manage and contain this invasive species effectively.

articles.title: NCW issues safety guidelines to step-up monitoring of app-based transport services
articles.summary: The National Commission for Women has released guidelines aimed at improving safety for women passengers using app-based transport services. These measures include verifying the background of drivers and ensuring proper identification matches. Additionally, the guidelines address issues related to late-night travel and unauthorized changes in drivers or vehicles. Aggregators are encouraged to create a verified pool of women drivers to enhance safety.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35m mansion: Why does it have a $1.75m twin in Illinois?
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion, Moyenage, has a fascinating architectural connection to a $1.75 million home in Wheaton, Illinois. Both properties were designed by architect Jarvis Hunt for steel magnate Jay C. Morse, with the Ohio estate reportedly based on his earlier Illinois residence. The 10,000-square-foot House of Seven Gables retains historic details, including fireplaces, oak panelling, beamed ceilings and carved woodwork, despite being relocated in 2017.

articles.title: Naomi Osaka’s family mission: How did her Haitian roots inspire her work?
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka's heartfelt bond with Haiti is rooted in her family's foundation, which was formed in 1999 to uplift the community. Her inaugural trip to Haiti occurred in October 2017, followed by another visit after her first Grand Slam win in 2018. Engaging with local children, she championed educational initiatives and allocated part of her earnings for earthquake relief. This connection deeply influences Osaka's ongoing philanthropic endeavors.

The court found the allegations against him to be vague and lacking necessary details. Justice Rajnesh Oswal ruled that his detention violated constitutional guarantees under Article 22(5). Shah had been accused of anti-national activities without sufficient evidence. Consequently, the court directed his immediate release if not wanted in other cases.

Masood's clear statements on the party's electoral strategy suggest underlying tensions that might define their coalition's effectiveness in challenging the BJP.

articles.title: Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies
articles.summary: Chirag Paswan's decision to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election marks an expansion of LJP (Ram Vilas). With plans to prepare for all 403 seats, the move could test the party's ability to build a Dalit vote base, influence close BJP-SP contests and strengthen its bargaining power within the NDA. His political journey from the 2020 Bihar split to a 19-seat win in 2025 provides the backdrop.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition targets Red Sea territory held by Houthis. What's Pak's role?
articles.summary: Islamabad has not publicly acknowledged direct involvement in Saudi Arabia's offensive inside Yemen. However, several reports point that Pakistani forces could be helping Saudi Arabia shift more of its military resources towards the war by taking over defensive responsibilities inside the kingdom. That could allow Saudi forces to concentrate on the offensive against the Houthis without Pakistan formally becoming a combatant in Yemen.

articles.title: BJP drops all 8 Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha members - what it means
articles.summary: The outgoing BJP members, apart from Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma, are Arun Singh, Neeraj Shekhar, Geeta Shakya, Brijlal and Seema Dwivedi. The eighth seat belonged to former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma, who resigned on September 11 after being appointed lieutenant governor (LG) of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. His term was due to end on November 25, like those of the others.

articles.summary: Short-term rentals have raised security concerns in residential societies, as unknown guests frequently enter and exit. Incidents like a fatal fall in an Airbnb apartment highlight the potential dangers associated with transient occupants. Many housing societies are now issuing warnings against such rentals due to ongoing security issues. Legal challenges are emerging as residents seek to enforce restrictions on short-term accommodations.

articles.title: Hyderabad tea stall owner walks into police station, sets himself ablaze
articles.summary: P Sudhakar, a tea stall owner in Bhimgal, attempted suicide by self-immolation at the local police station. He was agitated due to alleged threats from a rival grocery shop owner. The police had previously registered a petty case against him for violating late-night business hours. Immediate action by police personnel extinguished the flames, and he was taken to a government hospital for treatment.

The big question now is how to enable predictive systems to act on their own conclusions without drifting from business intent. The frontier has moved from prediction to autonomous decision making, and the gap between…

articles.title: 'Country moving in democratic way': BJP on SC notice to EC, govt on pleas against CEC
SC seeks EC response on changes during SIR: Why Form 6 has become a flashpoint
articles.summary: A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Bagchi and Mohana sought responses from the Election Commission, the Centre, the CEC and the other two election commissioners before examining whether the poll panel's statutory procedure was followed. The bench refused to pass an immediate order seeking the suspension of  CEC , while considering the controversy over Form 6, which was one of the central issues raised in the petitions.

articles.title: BJP announces 8 candidates for Rajya Sabha polls in UP; Puri, BL Verma not in list
articles.summary: BJP has announced eight candidates for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh. Union ministers Hardeep Puri and BL Verma were not included in this announcement. The election schedule was previously announced by the Election Commission of India. Meanwhile, the Samajwadi Party has designated two candidates for these polls as well. The final date for filing nominations will be October 6, followed by polling on October 16.

articles.title: 100 fighter jets part of op 'Yemen Dawn' to wrest Red Sea from Houthis
articles.summary: Saudi military spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said the coalition was providing “full operational support” to government forces. He said around 100 fighter jets were supporting the campaign and that the coalition had established “air protection” over the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The coalition also claimed to have destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets. Those claims, however, could not be independently verified.

articles.title: 2021 injury row: Mamata's lawyer sends notice to hospitals over record 'disclosure'
articles.summary: Mamata Banerjee's lawyer issued a legal notice to two hospitals over "unauthorised" medical record disclosures. This followed allegations made by West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari about her 2021 leg injury. Adhikari claimed that her injury was "faked" during the assembly elections, where she campaigned from a wheelchair. The notice sought clarification on how her medical records were revealed without permission.

articles.title: New Jersey data center spills 5,000 gallons of diesel; mayor cites 'computer glitch'
articles.summary: A New Jersey data center spilled thousands of gallons of diesel fuel into a tributary of the Hackensack River. The incident occurred on September 11 and involved a reported 5,000 gallons from a storage tank. Equinix confirmed that two broken valves caused the release while the mayor attributed it to a computer glitch. Clean-up crews removed about 3,500 gallons during the operation, without impacting local wildlife.

articles.title: 'Beaten to death by husband': 5-yr-old found playing with dolls beside mother’s body
articles.summary: In a tragic incident, a five-year-old girl was discovered playing near her mother's body in Vaishali district. The child's mother, Asha Devi, was reportedly beaten to death by her husband following a dispute. Family members learned of the incident after a neighbor alerted them about the situation. The police have initiated a search for Sujit, Asha's husband, who allegedly fled the scene.

articles.title: Man paid Rs 1.73 cr for Gurgaon flat, waited for a decade; commission orders refund + 12% interest
articles.summary: In 2012, the man booked the 2,600 sq ft apartment in a project located in Sector 83, Gurgaon. The basic sale price was fixed at Rs 6,428.50 per sq ft, apart from other applicable charges. The basic sale price of the apartment was stipulated at Rs 1.67 crore. Relying on the assurances given by the developer, the man obtained a home loan and ultimately paid Rs 1,72,93,048.76 towards the apartment.

articles.title: NEET UG among world’s 5 largest exams with 25 lakh applications
articles.summary: NEET UG has ranked as the world’s fifth-largest examination by applications, with around 25 lakh registrations, according to SBI Research. The report places China’s Gaokao at the top with 1.29 crore candidates. UPSC CSE, JEE Main and UGC NET also feature among major global examinations, highlighting the scale, security and contingency challenges involved in conducting tests for millions of candidates.

articles.title: France school protests: 15-year-old student loses hand in stun grenade incident
articles.summary: Protests in France have intensified due to teacher shortages, resulting in widespread school closures and clashes. A 15-year-old student lost his hand after handling a police stun grenade, prompting a government investigation. Police reported numerous arrests and significant property damage since the protests began last week. Student unions continue to organise demonstrations despite concerns over escalating violence.

articles.title: Giant pumpkin wins BC contest by just 1 pound after weighing 1,485 pounds
articles.summary: Kelowna grower Jordan Abbate won the 2026 B.C. Giant Pumpkin Contest with a 1,485-pound pumpkin, beating the runner-up by just one pound. The victory followed six months of daily care, including watering, pruning and soil preparation. The contest also saw two new B.C. records in other giant vegetable categories.

articles.title: 5,000-year-old Egyptian skulls reveal new evidence of retainer sacrifice
articles.summary: Researchers re-examininf 46 skulls excavated from Egypt’s First Dynasty royal cemetery at Abydos, found significant cranial trauma in 18 of them. The injuries provide new forensic evidence that some people buried around royal tombs may have been deliberately killed after a ruler’s death. The findings support the possibility of retainer sacrifice, although the exact cause of death remains uncertain for many others.

articles.title: Kansas neighbour cut 133 trees; court upholds $6,500 damages award
articles.summary: A Kansas appeals court has upheld a $6,500 damages award against a man whose neighbour’s fence project led to 133 trees being cut on adjoining land in 2015. The court found the landowner filed his trespass case within the legal time limit and that there was enough evidence to hold Douglas Black responsible for the tree damage.

articles.title: Microsoft co-founder gave $100M to brain research; his institute mapped 21,000 genes
articles.summary: Paul G. Allen invested $100 million in 2003 to establish the Allen Institute for Brain Science in Seattle. This institute focused on creating the Allen Brain Atlas, which mapped gene activity in the mouse brain. The Atlas revealed that approximately 80% of genes are active in the brain, surpassing previous estimates. The data from the project was made publicly available at no cost to researchers globally.

articles.title: Tiger Woods helps launch $2.5bn Texas golf community with 500 planned homes
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is helping launch Bluejack Ranch, a $2.5 billion, 914-acre gated golf community near Fort Worth, Texas. The project will have 500 homes, an 18-hole course, a dude ranch and resort-style amenities, with residential prices starting at $1 million.

articles.title: Gut bacteria may reveal how quickly your brain is ageing, study finds
articles.summary: A groundbreaking study by UCLA Health highlights the intriguing link between gut bacteria and brain ageing in healthy adults. Analyzing brain scans and gut health of nearly 1,500 participants, researchers identified a correlation between the Brain Ageing Index and certain gut microbes. This suggests that optimizing gut health may be pivotal for preserving cognitive function and offers an early detection path for interventions aimed at promoting healthier brain ageing.

articles.title: Travis Kelce-backed Six Flags: How is its $20.8M solar project going green?
articles.summary: Travis Kelce-backed Six Flags is making a major sustainability move as Magic Mountain’s new solar parking project powers two parks. The 12.37 MW installation covers 4,315 spaces and is expected to generate 20.8 million kWh annually. The project also includes an 8 MWh battery and 109 EV charging stations. Kelce joined Six Flags as a 2026 brand ambassador, adding star power to the company’s latest green initiative.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s Excel connection: Why is Linda Cohn questioning the WNBA?
articles.summary: Excel Search & Advisory is helping the NBA find Cathy Engelbert’s successor as WNBA commissioner. Because Excel Sports Management represents Caitlin Clark and Napheesa Collier, former ESPN host Linda Cohn has questioned how the company will separate its executive search work from player representation. The NBA has not publicly detailed specific safeguards, while Adam Silver remains involved in the final decision.

Residents are increasingly hesitant to enjoy these public spaces after sundown, as broken streetlights diminish safety and invite undesirable activities. Despite notifying the relevant authorities regarding these pressing concerns, timely improvements are desperately needed to restore community trust and ensure public safety in these areas.

articles.title: Customer challenged Rs 128 service charge at pub; court orders Rs 3,000 payout
articles.summary: A Bengaluru consumer commission has ruled in favor of a customer against Sherlock's Pub regarding a service charge. The customer, Rudresh, objected to a mandatory 7.5 percent service charge during his visit. He highlighted guidelines from the Central Consumer Protection Authority to the pub staff, yet was compelled to pay. The commission found the pub's enforcement of the charge to be a violation of consumer rights.

articles.title: 'Same thing could happen at World Cup': Karthik hails Rohit's measured 92 vs WI
articles.summary: In India's third ODI against the West Indies, Rohit Sharma displayed remarkable skill by scoring 92 runs amid challenging conditions. Following a string of early dismissals, he adopted a cautious approach before stepping on the gas. Former cricketer Dinesh Karthik hailed Rohit's experience as vital for upcoming international matches, particularly in South Africa, showcasing how seasoned players can thrive under pressure.

articles.title: Watch: Katihar lawyer cornered, shot in chest as attackers walk away calmly
articles.summary: Advocate Guddu Ansari, aged 35, was shot dead by armed assailants near Patel Chowk in Katihar district. The incident occurred around 9am and was captured on video, which is vital evidence for investigations. Local police are examining CCTV footage and the crime scene to identify the suspects involved in the murder. Investigators are also looking into a possible motive linked to an old dispute.

articles.title: Trio win Nobel prize for leap in optogenetics; how it unlocks brain's mysteries
articles.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine has been conferred upon Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for their pioneering work on light-gated ion channels and the innovative optogenetics technique. This advancement permits researchers to manipulate the activity of nerve cells in living brains, which holds promise for neuroscience and future medical treatments targeting visual impairments and various neural disorders.

articles.title: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper set to cut 24-hour journey to under 16
articles.summary: The country's second Vande Bharat sleeper service is expected to substantially reduce the time taken to travel by rail between Bengaluru, India's technology hub, and Mumbai, its financial capital. Although the official launch date has not yet been declared, the railway zones have been asked to commence the service at the earliest convenient opportunity.

articles.title: Congress MP and TVK MLA argue over lighting ceremonial lamp in govt event
articles.summary: During a baby shower event in Trichy, a disagreement arose between TVK MLA Navalpattu Viji and Congress MP Christopher Tilak. The conflict started over the protocol regarding who should light a ceremonial lamp first. After an argument, which escalated to Viji knocking the lamp from Tilak's hand, Minister Ramesh intervened to calm the situation. Viji ultimately lit the lamp after the disagreement was resolved.

BJP MLC Parinay Fuke criticized his comments and referred to his past experiences.

articles.title: Wyoming couple built off-grid home from 1,343 tyres; now listed for $625,000
articles.summary: A Wyoming Earthship built from 1,343 tyres in 2011 is now listed for $625,000. The 1,500-square-foot off-grid home sits on 55.13 acres and includes solar power, a wind turbine, rainwater collection and a 66-foot greenhouse.

articles.title: Denver Tudor estate built for $38,000 now lists for $10.75 million
articles.summary: An exquisite Tudor Revival estate, constructed in 1931, has hit the market in Denver for $10.75 million. Originally valued at $38,000, this historic home showcases remarkable architectural elements and expansive living areas. Its illustrious past includes ownership by renowned jeweler Tom Shane. With 10,370 square feet and beautifully landscaped gardens extending over three-quarters of an acre, this property is priced to reflect its status in Denver's luxury market.

articles.title: World’s oldest person asked doctors to study her body; cells told a different age
articles.summary: María Branyas Morera, who passed away at 117, lived an extraordinary life that captivated researchers. A novel analysis of her biological samples uncovered striking truths about her aging process, indicating a difference of about 23 years between her biological and chronological age. Her gut microbiome and blood composition contributed to her remarkable health, underscoring the impact of genetics and lifestyle choices on her impressive longevity.

Unfortunately, those alerts went unheeded, which led to a coordinated assault from Gaza, resulting in heavy casualties and numerous hostages. This incident has led to a critical examination of the systemic shortcomings within Israel's military intelligence operations.

articles.title: Why ICC fined India and West Indies after 3rd ODI in New Chandigarh
articles.summary: India and the West Indies were fined for slow over-rates in the third ODI, with India penalised 20 per cent and the visitors 10 per cent of their match fees. Both captains accepted the charges. West Indies ended the series on a high, chasing 352 behind Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162. The teams now turn to the five-match T20I series.

articles.title: Watch: US strike on vessel kills 4 'narco terrorists' in Caribbean
articles.summary: On Sunday, the US military executed a strike on a go-fast vessel in the Caribbean Sea. This operation resulted in the deaths of four individuals labeled as 'narco-terrorists'. The US Southern Command stated that the vessel was involved in narco-trafficking activities. Since September 2025, the US has intensified strikes on such vessels over narcotics smuggling allegations. Various human rights organizations have condemned these strikes as unlawful extrajudicial killings.
